dimension_1_licensing.summary: Broadest national-level license footprint in industry; MiCA CASP filed via Greece pending; VARA Dubai; ADGM; AUSTRAC; FIU-IND; JFSA.
dimension_1_licensing.detail: United States: Operates only via separate Binance.US entity. Parent Binance.com restricted from serving US persons following 2023 DOJ settlement. European Union: National-level DASP registrations in France (AMF E2022-037), Italy (OAM PSV5), Spain, Lithuania, Poland; MiCA CASP application filed via Greece (HCMC) January 2026, pending. United Arab Emirates: Dubai VASP license from VARA (2024); ADGM FSRA approval for Binance.com global platform via three regulated entities, operational from January 2026. Japan: Regulated under JFSA. Australia: AUSTRAC DCE registration via InvestbyBit Pty Ltd. India: FIU-IND reporting entity registration. Thailand: Digital Asset Operator licenses via Gulf Binance.
sources: Fortune, January 22, 2026, on Greek MiCA filing
dimension_1_licensing.notes: Broadest multi-jurisdictional license footprint by entity count. Breadth does not yet translate to unified MiCA CASP authorization. US standing constrained by 2023 DOJ settlement (Dimension 3).

dimension_2_travel_rule.summary: Implements Travel Rule across national-licensed entities; uses Notabene as primary technology partner.
dimension_2_travel_rule.detail: Binance has implemented Travel Rule compliance across its national-licensed entities (France, Italy, Spain, Lithuania for EU; AUSTRAC for Australia; FIU-IND for India). Uses Notabene as primary Travel Rule technology partner. Public statements confirm IVMS 101 support. US-side compliance is limited because Binance.com does not serve US customers post-2023 settlement.
dimension_2_travel_rule.notes: Travel Rule compliance footprint mirrors national licensing footprint. Strong in jurisdictions where licensed; gaps elsewhere.

dimension_3_sanctions_enforcement.category: Severe enforcement, resolved with ongoing constraints
dimension_3_sanctions_enforcement.summary: $4.3B DOJ settlement November 2023; CZ guilty plea and prison; ongoing 5-year compliance monitor through 2028.
dimension_3_sanctions_enforcement.detail: November 2023: DOJ settlement, $4.3 billion combined penalties (DOJ, FinCEN, OFAC, CFTC). Binance Holdings pleaded guilty to BSA violations, sanctions violations, unlicensed money transmission. CZ (founder, Changpeng Zhao) personally pleaded guilty, served prison time, paid $50M personal fine, banned from operational role. Ongoing 5-year compliance monitorship (DOJ-imposed) through 2028. Multiple jurisdictional restrictions: UK FCA (2021 marketing prohibition), Netherlands DNB exit (2023), various national restrictions historically.
dimension_3_sanctions_enforcement.notes: Largest single crypto exchange enforcement action in history. Compliance posture has materially strengthened post-settlement under new CEO Richard Teng. Ongoing DOJ monitor adds regulatory oversight layer that exceeds most peer exchanges.

dimension_5b_mixer_exposure.detail: Measured against Dune-labeled 'binance%' address set. Zero direct outflows or inflows to/from the four primary Tornado Cash ETH pools in 12-month window.

dimension_6_kyc_cdd.summary: Post-2023 DOJ settlement implemented mandatory global KYC; uses Sumsub and other vendors; under DOJ monitor through 2028.
dimension_6_kyc_cdd.detail: Following 2023 DOJ settlement, Binance implemented mandatory KYC across all account tiers globally (including markets where prior policy was permissive). Enhanced KYC for high-volume accounts. Use of Sumsub and other vendors for verification. Pre-2023 KYC posture was materially weaker - DOJ settlement specifically cited 'willful failure to maintain an effective AML program' as basis for $4.3B penalty. Post-settlement KYC remediation under 5-year DOJ monitor through 2028.
dimension_6_kyc_cdd.notes: Major historical KYC/CDD deficiencies; post-settlement program is materially stronger but the historical context is publicly known and remains relevant for risk assessment.

dimension_7_operational_track_record.summary: Founded 2017; SAFU insurance fund pioneer; covered $40M (2019) and $570M (2022) hack losses; orderly leadership transition CZ to Teng (2023).
dimension_7_operational_track_record.detail: Founded 2017; operating 9 years. 2019: $40M hot wallet hack (covered from Binance funds; SAFU insurance fund used for customer protection). 2022: $570M cross-chain bridge exploit (BSC bridge); Binance covered loss. 2023: Founder CZ stepped down as CEO following DOJ settlement; Richard Teng appointed CEO. Despite incidents, Binance's track record on covering customer losses has been strong (no customer haircuts).
dimension_7_operational_track_record.notes: Material historical incidents but customer protection track record is consistent. Leadership transition orderly.
